essentials.title: Log every visit to the secure exam storage
essentials.description: Every time anyone opens the secure storage, write down the date, time, person and purpose. The access log is one of the first things a Cambridge inspector asks for.

source.quote: Every single access is recorded: date, time, person, purpose. No gaps, no unsigned entries.

essentials.title: Check your calendar for the next Cambridge deadline
essentials.description: Look at your deadline calendar each week. Your own internal deadline should sit at least one week before each Cambridge deadline, so a problem can still be fixed in time.

source.quote: set your own internal deadline at least one week before each Cambridge deadline

essentials.title: File this week's exam records in your evidence file
essentials.description: Entry records, access-log pages, training registers, incident reports and dispatch receipts go into the evidence file in the week they are created. A gap you find yourself is a note; the same gap found by an inspector is a finding.

source.quote: File documents the week they are created, not in a pre-inspection scramble.

essentials.title: Check the official Cambridge date before you act on it
essentials.description: Dates in Eduversal documents are a planning guide. Before you register students or tell families a deadline, confirm it with Cambridge — the provider's official date always wins.

source.quote: The current official provider or government publication always takes precedence over this reference and over any Eduversal curriculum guide.

essentials.title: Write up any exam incident on the same day
essentials.description: If something goes wrong during an exam, the invigilator tells you, you decide with the Head of Centre where needed, and the incident report is written the same day. Suspected malpractice must reach Cambridge through the Head of Centre on the same day, or by 12:00 the next working day.

source.quote: everything is documented on the incident report the same day

tasks.title: Complete the safeguarding and security gate first
tasks.description: Finish the Eduversal safeguarding training and the security briefing (secure storage, access logs, Key Times). Your Principal records the date; you do not handle live entries or secure material before then.
tasks.applies_when: First exam cycle in the role
tasks.timing_text: Before you touch any live entry or secure material

source.quote: You do not handle live entries or secure material until Phase 0 training is complete and recorded.

tasks.title: Meet your guide, your Principal and your Quality Nominee
tasks.description: Go through the Exams Officer Handbook with your cross-school guide, agree a reading pace and walk through this year's Cambridge deadlines. If a previous Exams Officer is available, take a structured handover (access logs, entry status, open issues).
tasks.applies_when: First exam cycle in the role
tasks.timing_text: Before your first entry window

source.quote: A first call or visit to review the Exams Officer Handbook's 15-section structure together, agree a reading pace

tasks.title: Read one section of the Exams Officer Handbook
tasks.description: About ten minutes a week. After your first semester, use the handbook as a reference: each section maps to one phase of the exam cycle.
tasks.applies_when: First exam cycle in the role
tasks.timing_text: Every week of your first semester, starting the week after you meet your guide

source.quote: Read one section a week for your first semester (16 sections); after that, use it as a reference

tasks.title: Agree in writing who does what with the Cambridge Coordinator
tasks.description: When the two roles are held by different people, the Coordinator owns governance and strategy and the Exams Officer owns logistics and documentation. Put the split on paper so nothing is missed.
tasks.applies_when: Your school separates the Cambridge Coordinator and Exams Officer roles
tasks.timing_text: Start of the year

source.quote: Agree the split in writing at the start of the year so nothing falls between two chairs.

tasks.title: Build this year's Cambridge deadline calendar
tasks.description: Put both series (October/November and May/June) and the Checkpoint series in one calendar: entries, access arrangements, Key Times, results and post-results deadlines. Add your internal deadline a week before each one and record it in your school's exam operations annex.
tasks.timing_text: Start of the year

source.quote: Take the Cambridge dates for the year, put them in your calendar

tasks.title: Make sure every teacher can log in to the Support Hub
tasks.description: Teachers use the Cambridge School Support Hub for past papers, mark schemes and examiner reports, and they come to you for an account. The school's centre registration entitles all teaching staff to one.
tasks.timing_text: Start of the year, then whenever a teacher asks

source.quote: If you do not have SSH access, request it from your school's Cambridge Exams Officer or Cambridge Coordinator.

tasks.title: Check which of your subjects are e-marked this year
tasks.description: For e-marked subjects you scan and upload every script within 48 hours. Make sure the scanner, internet connection and trained staff are ready before the first series.
tasks.timing_text: Start of the year

source.quote: Check the annual updates for which of your subjects are e-marked; the list grows every year.

tasks.title: Submit the October/November entries before 16 August 2026
tasks.description: Review every entry twice (names exactly as on the passport), get the Head of Centre's approval, then submit in Cambridge International Direct. The Grades 9–10 structure gives 16 August 2026 for November IGCSE entries and 21 September 2026 for retakes from June 2026; confirm every deadline, including AS Level entries, with Cambridge.
tasks.timing_text: Cambridge deadline 16 August 2026 — submit by your internal deadline a week earlier

source.quote: Confirm November 2026 IGCSE entry — the Cambridge deadline is 16 August 2026.

tasks.title: Ask your guide to review your entries before you submit
tasks.description: In your first cycle, your guide checks your entries, room plans and access-arrangement requests before they go to Cambridge. A mistake caught together is the process working, not a failure.
tasks.applies_when: First exam cycle in the role
tasks.timing_text: Before each entry deadline

source.quote: Draft your first entries; your guide reviews them before you submit.

tasks.title: Release the results and lead the analysis with the Principal
tasks.description: Download the Statement of Results with the Head of Centre and give each candidate their statement securely — never post results publicly. Then compare results with predicted grades, global benchmarks and last year, and share subject reports with Heads of Department.
tasks.timing_text: May/June results: early-to-mid August; October/November results: mid-January — Cambridge's official release date wins

source.quote: You and the Head of Centre download the Statement of Results from CID and distribute individual statements to candidates securely.

tasks.title: Manage post-results requests by each Cambridge deadline
tasks.description: Handle clerical re-checks, reviews of marking and return of scripts (enquiries about results) with families and teachers. Advise honestly: a review of marking can move a grade down as well as up.
tasks.timing_text: Deadlines are typically about three weeks after results — check Cambridge's dates

source.quote: Post-results services — manage requests in consultation with families and subject teachers

tasks.title: Check the Outstanding Cambridge Learner Awards
tasks.description: Cambridge chooses the winners from the results; schools do not nominate. Verify any recipients on Cambridge's official list before the school celebrates or announces anything.
tasks.timing_text: After the results and Cambridge's awards release (suggested weeks)

source.quote: the Exams Officer should check the official Outstanding Cambridge Learner Awards information, verify any recipients

tasks.title: Lead the post-series review with the Quality Nominee
tasks.description: Look at the incident log, stakeholder feedback and where procedures creaked. Send the Principal a short review report with updated procedures, training needs and budget recommendations.
tasks.timing_text: September for the May/June series; March for the October/November series

source.quote: After each series — September for May/June, March for Oct/Nov — you and the Quality Nominee lead a structured review

tasks.title: Destroy leftover papers once the post-results window closes
tasks.description: Cross-shred unused question papers and leftover scripts only after the post-results window has closed, and keep a destruction log signed off by the Principal.
tasks.timing_text: After the post-results window closes (suggested weeks)

source.quote: Unused question papers and leftover scripts are securely destroyed — cross-shredded — only after the post-results window closes

tasks.title: Prepare the October/November series
tasks.description: Entries are closed, so the work now is access arrangements, the final timetable and clashes, secure materials and invigilation. Check your Key Times on the Cambridge website, and remember some papers fall in EASE Week 1 and in the TKA window (26 October–8 November).
tasks.timing_text: Early September — papers start in late September

source.quote: The focus then shifts to access arrangements, timetables, secure materials, invigilation and clash management

tasks.title: Check, sign for and lock away the secure materials
tasks.description: When a delivery arrives, check the seals and the contents against the dispatch list, sign and date the receipt and store everything at once. If a seal is broken, stop and contact Cambridge the same day.
tasks.timing_text: When materials arrive, in the weeks before each series

source.quote: verify package integrity (seals intact, no damage), check contents against the dispatch list, sign and date the receipt, store everything immediately

tasks.title: Train and brief your invigilators before the series
tasks.description: Brief every invigilator, including temporary or external staff who have passed safeguarding checks, on the rules and on any access arrangements they will deliver. Rehearse a fire alarm, a sick candidate and a phone found, and re-read the exams contingency plan.
tasks.timing_text: The week before each series starts

source.quote: Run a short scenario briefing with invigilators before every series: fire alarm, sick candidate, phone found.

tasks.title: Set up the exam rooms
tasks.description: Desks at least 1.25 metres apart, a seating plan by candidate number, a clock everyone can see and silence signs on the doors. Prepare a separate room for students with approved access arrangements.
tasks.timing_text: Before each series starts

source.quote: Desks at least 1.25 metres apart in all directions, measured centre-to-centre.

tasks.title: Contact your guide the same day if anything goes wrong
tasks.description: Share your exam-day timetable with your guide. If there is a timing issue, a security concern or anything unusual, follow the school's incident procedure and also tell your guide that day.
tasks.applies_when: First exam cycle in the role
tasks.timing_text: Before and during each series

source.quote: If an incident occurs — a timing issue, a security concern, anything outside the routine — you contact your guide the same day

tasks.title: Check the Entry Confirmation Report against your approved list
tasks.description: Verify every student and subject on Cambridge's Entry Confirmation Report, then tell students and parents their confirmed entries and fees.
tasks.timing_text: When Cambridge returns the report after each entry deadline

source.quote: Cambridge returns an Entry Confirmation Report — you verify every student and subject against your approved list

tasks.title: Run this week's exam days and send the scripts on time
tasks.description: Bring the sealed packets to the room just before each exam, visit rooms unannounced and stay reachable while an exam runs. Count scripts against the register and dispatch them within 2 working days (uploads for e-marking within 48 hours).
tasks.timing_text: Exam weeks: late September to mid-November 2026 (papers also run in EASE Week 1, 28 Sep–2 Oct) and from late April 2027 — follow the Cambridge final timetable

source.quote: deliver packets to the exam room just before the exam starts, make unannounced visits to check invigilation quality

tasks.title: Run the October 2026 Checkpoint sitting for last year's Grade 8
tasks.description: Students who finished Grade 8 in May 2026 keep their planned October 2026 Lower Secondary Checkpoint sitting — the last cohort on the October arrangement. Checkpoint is windowed, so Key Times do not apply; confirm the test window with Cambridge.
tasks.timing_text: October 2026 Checkpoint series — confirm the dates with Cambridge

source.quote: Students who completed Grade 8 in May 2026 retain the previously planned October 2026 Checkpoint sitting.

tasks.title: Send the data for the Annual Examinations Report
tasks.description: Give the Principal the figures on participation, outcomes, compliance, incidents and budget. The Principal presents the report.
tasks.timing_text: November

source.quote: Each November the Board receives an Annual Examinations Report: participation, outcomes, compliance status, incidents, and budget.

tasks.title: Check and hand over the Cambridge certificates
tasks.description: Certificates arrive about three months after results. Check each one against the results data, and log every handover with a signature.
tasks.timing_text: About three months after each results release

source.quote: Verify each certificate against results data before distributing; log every handover with a signature

tasks.title: Open the access arrangements list for the next cohort
tasks.description: Collecting diagnostic evidence takes months, so start the term before entries, alongside subject selection. Work with the learning support / SEN coordinator, and think about safeguarding when you plan each arrangement.
tasks.timing_text: The term before each entry window

source.quote: Open the access arrangements list for a cohort the term before entries — together with subject selection.

tasks.title: Submit the access arrangement applications for the next series
tasks.description: Send each application with its evidence before Cambridge's published deadline, and apply again every series — approval does not carry over. Keep an implementation log so each arrangement actually happens in the exam room.
tasks.timing_text: By Cambridge's published deadline for each series (suggested weeks — the live documents give no date)

source.quote: Most need an application to Cambridge, with evidence, by the published deadline for each series

tasks.title: Submit March 2027 Checkpoint entries by 27 November 2026
tasks.description: Only for a March sitting already agreed with Eduversal in advance; May is the network series. Late entries close 14 December 2026.
tasks.applies_when: Your school has an agreed March 2027 Checkpoint exception
tasks.timing_text: Final entries deadline 27 November 2026 — confirm with Cambridge

source.quote: If March 2027 series: final entries deadline 27 November 2026.

tasks.title: Review the examinations policy with the Quality Nominee and Principal
tasks.description: Update the policy with what the October/November series taught you. Keep version control and a change log.
tasks.timing_text: Once a year, after the October/November series

source.quote: The examinations policy itself is reviewed annually — by you, the Quality Nominee, and the Principal, after the Oct/Nov series

tasks.title: Walk the inspection readiness checklist
tasks.description: Cambridge can inspect at any time, announced or not. Check that storage logs are signed, training records are current, declarations are submitted and malpractice files are in order.
tasks.timing_text: Once a term (suggested weeks)

source.quote: Once a term, walk the inspection readiness checklist: storage logs complete and signed, training records current, declarations submitted, malpractice files in order.

tasks.title: Audit the secure storage and log the audit
tasks.description: Check the locks, the key holders (two or three, no spare keys) and that every entry in the access log is complete. Record the audit itself in the log.
tasks.timing_text: Once a month

source.quote: Audit your own storage monthly and log the audit.

tasks.title: Keep your Exams Officer training up to date
tasks.description: Plan your Cambridge refresher webinars and the Eduversal network training, and file the certificates. If you are new, complete the Cambridge Exams Officer course within six months of appointment.
tasks.timing_text: Suggested check: early each semester

source.quote: Attend at least two Cambridge refresher webinars each year, and the Eduversal network training sessions held twice annually

tasks.title: Prepare the May/June 2027 entries
tasks.description: Collect the subject combinations approved by the Principal or Academic Coordinator for Grade 10 IGCSE and approved A Level continuation candidates, plus every Grade 6 and Grade 8 Checkpoint candidate. Check names character by character against passports or ID.
tasks.timing_text: Start of Semester 2

source.quote: Your role: supply accurate information about what the school can offer, and record the approved list.

tasks.title: Submit the May/June 2027 entries, including both Checkpoints
tasks.description: Primary (Grade 6) and Lower Secondary (Grade 8) Checkpoint final entries close around 21 February 2027 (late around 11 March), and June 2027 IGCSE entries are due around February. Confirm every exact date in Cambridge International Direct; the Head of Centre approves before you submit.
tasks.timing_text: Around 21 February 2027 — confirm the exact Cambridge dates

source.quote: for the May 2027 series, final entries close around 21 February 2027

tasks.title: Check the May Checkpoint timetable against the May holidays
tasks.description: As soon as Cambridge publishes the timetable, check it with the Principal against Idul Adha (17 May), cuti bersama (18–19 May) and Waisak (20 May). Report any conflict to Eduversal at once.
tasks.timing_text: As soon as Cambridge publishes the timetable (suggested week)

source.quote: The Cambridge Exam Officer confirms the exact Checkpoint timetable against the public holidays of 17–20 May with the Principal

tasks.title: Prepare the Cambridge Centre Annual Declaration
tasks.description: Prepare the declaration for the Principal to sign and file the signed copy in your evidence file.
tasks.timing_text: Typically by March

source.quote: The signed Cambridge Centre Annual Declaration — you prepare it, the Principal signs it, typically by March

tasks.title: Prepare the May/June 2027 series
tasks.description: Check your Key Times, confirm the final timetable and solve clashes, and plan every approved access arrangement and exam room — including Primary Checkpoint logistics with the Grade 6 team. IGCSE papers start around 24 April 2027.
tasks.timing_text: Early April, before the series begins

source.quote: Check your Key Times on the Cambridge website before each series

tasks.title: Plan what continues after teaching ends on 7 May
tasks.description: The series runs on after the last teaching week: the Checkpoint window (around 11–21 May), IGCSE papers to around 9 June and A Level papers. Keep staff on the invigilation rota, the secure storage routine and 2-working-day dispatch going; results follow in early-to-mid August and the post-series review in September.
tasks.timing_text: Last teaching week — before the May/June series continues without lessons

source.quote: IGCSE June-series papers continue to ~9 Juni, after year-end — schools must staff June invigilation.

tasks.title: Hold your Readiness Checkpoint with your Principal and guide
tasks.description: Review the full cycle together — entries, exam days, results and your evidence file — and write a short, honest reflection. The outcome is Certified or Extended, never a score.
tasks.applies_when: First exam cycle in the role
tasks.timing_text: At the end of your first complete cycle — agree the date with your Principal and guide

source.quote: Pre-conference: you, your Principal, and your guide review the full cycle together — entries, exam days, results, and your evidence file.

tasks.title: Ask your guide to review your results and dispatch paperwork
tasks.description: Before you close your first series, your guide checks your dispatch records and how you handled results. Build that series' evidence file at the same time.
tasks.applies_when: First exam cycle in the role
tasks.timing_text: After your first series' results

source.quote: Your guide reviews your dispatch paperwork and your results-handling process before you close out the cycle.

notes_for_reviewer: Role assignment: CC2-015 (centre status), CC2-028 (exam rooms), CC2-047 (SSE), CC2-048 (coursework/moderation) and CC2-049 (predicted grades) are anchored to the Cambridge Compliance / Operations items of the School Principals Checklist, which is addressed to principals and academic coordinators. They are included because the brief asked for them and the Exams Officer Handbook gives the operational work (rooms, entries, records) to the Exams Officer, but no live document names the Exams Officer as owner of the SSE or of predicted-grade review. CC2-047 and CC2-049 are marked 'recommended' for that reason. Please confirm or move them to the Principal list.

Not included (Principals Checklist only, no Exams Officer basis): 'Track the school's annual Cambridge subscription and registration renewal' and 'Prepare for and host any scheduled Cambridge Associate or support visits'.

No live Academic Services document gives an access-arrangements deadline. CC2-037 is placed in suggested weeks (late July for Oct/Nov, early March for May/June). v1 cited ES 10.3 (1 March) — the ES corpus is not part of the exported pack, so it was not used. Consider adding the current Cambridge access-arrangement deadlines to 'Quality Ecosystem: External Exams & Admissions 26-27'.

No live document gives the AS Level October/November 2026 entry deadline; only the November 2026 IGCSE deadline (16 August 2026, retakes 21 September 2026) appears, in the Grades 09-10 Structure. CC2-018 tells the reader to confirm AS entries with Cambridge.

Calendar conflict: 'Curriculum Module: Grades 04-06 Structure' says the last teaching day is 12 May 2027 ("Last teaching day 12 Mei" and "last teaching day on 12 May 2027"); the network calendar and the Grades 07-08 Structure say 7 May 2027. CC2-052 uses 7 May.

Calendar conflict: Cambridge papers start in EASE Week 1 (28 Sep–2 Oct 2026, a non-teaching week in the checklist calendar) — AS General Paper 28–30 Sep, Chemistry practical 29 Sep, IGCSE November series from 28 Sep. No checklist week exists for those exam days; CC2-032 shows in the week of 21 Sep with a note.
The October 2026 Lower Secondary Checkpoint transition sitting (CC2-033) has no test dates in any live document; it is placed in the first October teaching week.

Handbook inconsistency: the Exams Officer Handbook has 16 sections ("Read one section a week for your first semester (16 sections)") while the Exams Officer Induction says "15-section structure" and "the full 15-section operational manual".
Naming inconsistency for Checkpoint exceptions: Grades 04-06 says exceptions are agreed with the 'Academic and Curriculum Division'; Grades 07-08 says the 'Academic Board'. CC2-038 says 'Eduversal'.

'Each November the Board receives an Annual Examinations Report' (CC2-034) does not say which board (school governance or the Eduversal Academic Board). The task text says only 'the Principal presents the report', as the Handbook does.
The inspection-readiness walk is 'once a term' in the Handbook; the network uses semesters, so CC2-040 is placed once per semester in suggested weeks.
The May/June 2027 results (early-to-mid August 2027), their post-results services and certificates fall in AY 2027-2028 and are not placed here; the August 2026 and January 2027 releases are.

2026-10-02 review: CC2-015 (centre status), CC2-047 (SSE), CC2-048 (coursework/moderation) and CC2-049 (predicted grades) removed — the live documents give these to the Principal / Academic Coordinator (School Principals Checklist) or the Quality Nominee (Exams Officer Handbook), not the Exams Officer. CC2-028 re-anchored to Exams Officer Handbook §7.

ideas_not_in_live_docs.idea: A weekly habit of reading Cambridge updates (centre bulletins, timetable changes, syllabus notices) and passing on what matters.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.why_useful: The live documents only mention the annual e-marking update and annual syllabus circulars; Cambridge bulletins land throughout the year.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.suggested_live_doc: Curriculum Module: Exams Officer Handbook 26-27 (Section 15 or 16)

ideas_not_in_live_docs.idea: Typical network dates for May/June entries (15 February) and access-arrangement applications (1 March).
ideas_not_in_live_docs.why_useful: v1 took these from ES 10.3; the Academic Services pack gives Checkpoint dates but no access-arrangement deadline at all.
